name: The example
why: 3: replace k with s, replace e with i, insert g at the end.

name: From nothing
why: 3: insert all three letters. This is row 0 of the table.

name: To nothing
why: 3: delete all three letters. This is column 0 of the table.

name: The same
why: 0: the words are already equal, so no change is needed.

name: Horse to ros
why: 3: replace h with r, delete r, delete e.

name: Intention to execution
why: 5: for example delete i, change n to e, change t to x, insert c, change n to u. Each delete, insert or change costs 1.

name: Shifted by one
why: 2: delete a at the front and insert q at the end. Replacing all 16 letters would cost 16.

name: Nothing in common, 14 letters
why: 14: replace every letter. Plain recursion tries three choices at every mismatch, millions of calls for 14 letters. There are only 15 × 15 different pairs of prefixes.

name: 1,000 letters each
args: (''.join('abcd'[(k * k * 7 + k * 3 + 1) % 11 % 4] for k in range(1000)), ''.join('abcd'[(k * k * 13 + k * 5 + 1) % 11 % 4] for k in range(1000)))
why: A table of 1,001 × 1,001 cells, filled row by row. Keep two rows if you like; the answer is the bottom-right cell. Memoised recursion fails here: this input needs far more nested calls than Python allows (about 1,000, and only a few hundred with functools.cache in the browser). Fill a table with a loop instead (lesson 3).

name: Different lengths
args: (''.join('abcd'[(k * k * 5 + k * 1 + 1) % 11 % 4] for k in range(1000)), ''.join('abcd'[(k * k * 3 + k * 7 + 1) % 11 % 4] for k in range(400)))
why: At least 600: the longer string must lose 600 letters.
